reason: VALUE/TRANSFER lens. The mechanism is sound: it is subtractive, nodes are untouched (no node-multiplier artefact), it does not trust in-sample network confidence, and each removed evaluable FP fork is worth 0.1*J/D (+0.0004..+0.0015 public), as claimed. The idea's ceiling is inflated, though, and the realistic gain is below +0.002 and below LB resolution. (1) Wrong fraction. '25% of 43 FP' is the 4.0 um figure (11 FP/0 TP). At the 4.5 um threshold actually proposed, the exp39 audit removes 6 FP/0 TP = 14% (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_research_fork-midpoint-filter.json). On the dorado-like 44b6 it removes <=1 of 10 FP. Lab score at 4.5 = 23/194 -> 23/188 = +0.0004. (2) x138 adds no new headroom. Its safe-div gates are identical to exp39/exp48 (9/14/0.6/2.25/10/0.0076/0.00375; only DeepCenter 0.25 vs 0.20, no DivNet veto; the division geometry filter is off: experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb cell 0 and line ~247). The claim that x138 'carries none of our fork hygiene' is empty, because exp48/51 never shipped forkmid either. The exp39 audit is the best proxy, and it does not grow on x138. (3) Metric arithmetic. Division J is pooled (tools/official/metrics.md l.142). The expected gain has the closed form 0.1*f*J*(1-J/r), where r is public recall. J_pub 0.36 at precision p means 1/r = 1/J + 1 - 1/p. The safe-div funnel passes only 35/151 GT divisions even on GT coordinates in the lab, so r > 0.55 is implausible. Public precision must therefore be >= ~0.5, and public FP forks are ~0.3-0.4*G, about 5-15, not 5-40. FP count and per-FP value are anti-correlated, so the idea's '10 removed x high per-FP value' corner does not exist. (4) Monte Carlo (J 0.28-0.38, G 15-50, r <= 0.55, f 0.03-0.20, per-TP loss 0.2-3% for unvalidated head coordinates): mean +0.0004..+0.0005, p10 -0.0016, p90 +0.0023, P(>= +0.002) 0.13-0.14, P(< 0) 0.17-0.18. A 1.2-1.5 FP expected removal vs. a ~20% chance of losing one TP (= -0.001..-0.002). Only if f = 25% (the 4.0 fraction) does the mean reach +0.0026. At 4.0 on head coordinates the TP margin is 0.24 um vs a 0.74 um mean head shift, so that is not safe either. (5) Transfer. The thresholds were read off all 199 in-sample videos, and 10 of 11 removed FP come from 6bba (one embryo). They are mostly z-offset FPs, and z is the axis the V1284 head re-localises. No x138 lab cache exists, and none can be measured in this container. LB noise is ~0.003, and bundling it with the ladder makes it unattributable. It is a rider at best, not a scored gain toward 0.99.
